default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun「みせ」that comes right after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle「は」raises「みせ」the store as the main topic discussed in the whole sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle「が」marks the object directly described by the adjective「すくない」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い「すくない」combines with「です」to form a polite predicate describing the small quantity of goods.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses the structure for describing an attribute「N1 は N2 が A」. Here,「このみせ」is the main topic placed at the beginning of the sentence by「は」. The component「品物」is the specific object being described and goes with the particle「が」, while the adjective「すくない」serves as the predicate at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If「少し」is used, it is an adverb of quantity (meaning “a little”) and cannot go directly with「です」to form an adjective predicate in place of「少ない」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If「あまりない」is used, the sentence changes to the negative form “there are not very many goods,” which sounds gentler than「少ない」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse the adverb「少し」(a little) with the adjective「少ない」(few), so they use the wrong predicate structure「少しです」instead of「少ないです」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: I will enter a university in Japan in April.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle「に」comes after a specific time point「4月」to show when the action takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle「の」connects two nouns and modifies the noun「だいがく」that follows it to show origin or location.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle「に」shows the destination of the action of entering the university「入学する」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb「入学する」is changed into the polite form「します」and serves as the main predicate, showing an action that will happen in the future.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The time expression「4月に」is placed at the beginning to set the time point. It is followed by the modifying phrase「日本の だいがくに」, which identifies the place or goal. The verb「入学します」comes at the end and combines with the particle「に」to show the destination of entering the university.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If「入る」is used, the sentence has a normal conversational meaning (“go into university”), while「入学する」is formal and precise vocabulary for the enrollment procedure.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If「通う」is used, it means going to school regularly every day, not starting university enrollment.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often use the particle「で」because they translate the phrase “enter a school in” directly from Vietnamese. However, with「入学する」, the particle「に」must be used to show the destination.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: I go to school by train.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で comes after a means of transportation to show how someone travels.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of regular travel.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 通う is changed into the form ています to show repeated travel, such as going to school or work, as a habit.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The particle で shows the means of travel (train), the particle に shows the destination (school), and 通っています shows that the person goes to school regularly every day.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It only means going to school or attending school now, without emphasizing regular, frequent travel like 通う.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle で (means of transportation) with に (destination), or translate “go to school” as 学校へ行く and forget the verb 通う, which is specially used for going to school or work regularly.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks 日本 as the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects two nouns and modifies the noun くに that follows it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun combines with です to form an affirmative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The sentence follows the definition structure A is B (AはBです). In this structure, the phrase 工業のくに is connected by the particle の to modify the noun くに.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because 工業 is a noun, not an adjective ending in な, so it must be connected with の.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often mistake field nouns, such as 工業 and 農業, for adjectives ending in な. They then incorrectly use 工業な instead of 工業の.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks バス as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に comes after a time point with a specific number to show when the action happens.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The Group 3 verb 出発する is changed into the polite form します and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The topic バス comes at the beginning with the particle は. It is followed by a specific time point with に and ends with the verb 出発します to express the departure schedule.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle is wrong because a specific time point must go with に, not the object marker を.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add the particle に after specific numbered time points, such as hours, dates, and months.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: I exercise every day to stay healthy.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The structure N のために shows the purpose of an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb of frequency modifies the verb 運動しています in the predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 運動する is changed into the form ています to show an action that continues and repeats as a habit.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The purpose phrase (けんこうのために) comes at the beginning to state the goal. It is followed by the frequency adverb まいにち and the predicate 運動しています, which describe the habit of continuing to exercise.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It changes the sentence into a comparison meaning “like health,” which completely loses the meaning of purpose.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: When combined with a noun, the pattern ために must include the particle の (N のために). Learners often forget this particle の.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object directly affected by the transitive verb 閉める.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The structure Vてもいいですか is used to ask the listener for permission to perform an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The object まど with を is the object of the transitive verb 閉める. It combines with the permission pattern 〜てもいいですか to politely ask the other person’s opinion.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It changes into a request meaning “Please close the window” (the listener does it), instead of the speaker asking permission to close it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes into a question about obligation: “Do I have to close the window?” rather than a request for permission.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the subject of the action in the pattern 〜てもいいですか (the speaker asks for permission to do it) with the pattern 〜てください (the listener is asked to do it).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: Please go straight along this road.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun 道 that comes right after it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を goes with the movement verb 行く to show the route or space through which the action passes.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb shows the manner of movement and directly modifies the verb 行ってください.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く is changed into the form て and combines with ください to give a polite instruction or request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The demonstrative この modifies 道. The particle を marks the space along which one moves. The adverb まっすぐ modifies the manner of the guiding predicate 行ってください.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle is wrong because when moving along a road or through a space, the particle を must be used, not に.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The particle へ turns “road” into the destination rather than the route along which one travels.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often only know the particle を as a marker for an affected object and forget that を also goes with movement verbs (行く, 歩く, 渡る) to show the route or space one passes through.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: Would you like to go see a movie together tomorrow?
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.sk: N(time) ＋ 副詞 ＋ N を ＋ V(remove ます) に ＋ 行きませんか
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing when the action happens, with a comma to create a pause at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb shows the manner of doing an action together with another person.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of watching.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the ます form, with ます removed, combines with the particle に to show the purpose of movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The movement verb in the negative-question form ませんか is used to make a polite invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.cn: Vます(remove ます) / N ＋ に行く・に来る
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The sentence is used to invite the other person to do something together. The structure V(remove ます) + に + 行きます shows the purpose of movement. It combines with the negative-question ending ませんか to form a polite invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It sounds more like a suggestion for the speaker to do something alone or together actively, and less like carefully asking for the other person’s opinion with 〜ませんか.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It is simply a statement informing someone that the speaker is going to see a movie; it is not an invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle に with を or で when expressing the purpose of an action involving movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: I borrow a book from a friend.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.sk: N(person) に + N(thing) を + かります
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に is used with the verb かります to indicate the source person from whom we receive or borrow something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object being borrowed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate ends the sentence in the polite form and expresses the action of borrowing something from another person.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The verb かります (borrow) takes the source object through the particle に (or から) to indicate the person lending the item, and the particle を to indicate the thing being borrowed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It means to lend, when the speaker gives something to another person to use, opposite to かります.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Use から instead of に to emphasize the starting point—the act of receiving the book from a friend. The meaning is equivalent.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse かします (lend) with かります (borrow).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the verb 聞く.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の turns the action 聞く into a noun. Together with the particle が, it goes with the adjective すき to show the object of liking.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in な expresses feelings or preferences and forms the main predicate at the end of a polite sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: Because すきです is an adjective that requires a noun before it as its complement, the verb 聞く must be turned into a noun with the particle の, followed by the particle が to show the object of liking.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses talent or skill in doing an action, rather than a preference.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It also turns a verb into a noun, but in spoken language, の is more natural and common when combined with すき/きらい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add the particle の to turn the verb into a noun before がすきです, and incorrectly use 聞くがすきです.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + のがすきだ / すきです
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: It will be finished soon, so please wait a little longer.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that something will happen immediately afterward.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjunction particle から follows the plain form to state a cause or reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing an additional amount, degree, or period of time.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern V-て + ください is used to make a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: The first clause uses the conjunction particle から to give an objective reason—that something will soon be finished—which provides the basis for the polite request in the second clause, with the structure Vて + ください.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It states a more objective and formal reason than から and sounds gentler and more polite.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This is a much more polite and gentle way to make a request than てください.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the て conjugation of Group 1 verbs: まつ changes to まって with a doubled consonant, not まちて.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形 + から / Vて + ください
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: There was a fire near the station yesterday.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.sk: N(time) + N の + N(place) で + N(event) が + ありました
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time adverb referring to the past, placed at the beginning of the sentence to set the time background.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の links a place noun to the location noun ちかく that it modifies.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where an event or incident, such as a fire, occurs.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject or event that occurs and goes with the verb あります.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-tense verb あります means to occur or take place when used with an event or accident.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: N(place) で + N(event) が + ある / あります
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: When expressing that an event, incident, or accident, such as a fire or festival, occurs somewhere, Japanese uses the place particle で and the verb あります to show that it takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Use に when talking about the fixed location where an object exists, not an event or incident that takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Use the verb おきました (occur) for a more formal and news-like style.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often use the particle に instead of で when they see the verb あります. The rule is: use に for objects that exist, and で for events that occur.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: The bus is coming soon. Please hurry.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that something will happen shortly.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the verb 来ます.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 来ます combines with the sentence-final modal particle よ to give the listener new information and remind them of it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern V-て + ください is used to ask or urge someone to act quickly.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the particle よ to announce and remind the listener that the bus will arrive soon. This creates the necessary context for the second sentence, which makes an urgent request with Vて + ください.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It means “let us hurry together” rather than asking the other person to hurry.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: A direct command from a superior to a subordinate, with a forceful and less polite tone.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the て conjugation of Group 1 verbs ending in ぎ: いそぎます changes to いそいで, not いそぎて.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: Because I passed the exam, I am in a very good mood.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the object of passing, ごうかくする.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: A polite past-tense verb combines with the conjunction particle から to state a cause or reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が follows a noun to show that it is the subject with the quality or state described by the predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い serves as the main predicate and ends the polite sentence with です.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses the structure “N に ごうかくする” with the conjunction から to state the reason. The second clause uses “きぶんがいい” to express a happy, comfortable feeling.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It states an objective reason in a gentler and more formal polite way than から.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Do not use the particle を with ごうかくする. Use N に ごうかくする instead.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: Please spread butter on the bread.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に indicates the surface that receives the spreading or applying action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ぬる is conjugated into the て form to combine with the request pattern.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: It follows a verb in the て form to create a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: The verb ぬる (spread, apply) goes with the particle に for the receiving surface (N1) and を for the substance being spread (N2). It combines with the てください form to create a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this when asking or advising someone not to do an action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle に, meaning the place where something is applied, with で, meaning a means or tool.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: This research took five years and was finally completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase with the particle 「は」 states the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 「かかる」 uses the 「て」 form to connect the clause showing the time spent before completion.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing that an expected result was achieved after a long period of effort.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The intransitive verb 「おわる」 uses the polite past tense as the predicate that closes the event.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The topic is placed at the beginning with 「は」, followed by a dependent clause in the 「〜て」 form to state the time that passed. This creates a basis for the adverb 「やっと」 to highlight the relief felt when the work was finished.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means 'in the end,' but it can be used for negative results as well, while やっと is used only when an expected result is achieved after much difficulty.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It has a more formal, written tone when describing a major turning point after a long period.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: The adverb 「やっと」 expresses relief at achieving the desired result. Avoid using it for random events or bad results.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: I returned to my country after a long time.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of time describing an action that happens again after a long period without happening.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に is used with a noun showing the destination or endpoint of movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past tense (ました).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The adverb ひさしぶりに is placed at the beginning of the sentence and modifies the entire movement predicate. It combines with the particle に to clearly identify the destination of the verb かえる.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle へ emphasizes the direction of movement, while に emphasizes the final destination.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add the particle に after ひさしぶり when modifying a verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: The ship arrived at the port.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action of arriving at the port.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the destination reached by the verb meaning 'to arrive.'
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate is in the polite past tense and shows that the action was completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: The sentence describes the ship, whose subject is marked by が, moving to and arriving at its destination, the port, which is marked by に.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If で (みなとで) is used, the sentence means that the action takes place inside the port area instead of arriving at the port.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If へ (みなとへ) is used, the sentence emphasizes movement in the direction of the port rather than the actual destination reached.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particles に and で when indicating the destination of verbs such as 到着する (とうちゃくする) or つく.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the topic being explained: the hobby.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of reading.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun こと to turn the action into a noun.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The noun phrase with です functions as the predicate and defines the content of the topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: This sentence pattern uses 'こと' to nominalize a verb and create a corresponding noun clause, which clearly defines the content of the topic 'hobby'.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If '〜の本を読むのです' is used, the sentence takes on an explanatory tone and gives a reason instead of defining the hobby.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the verb to its dictionary form before こと and keep the ending ます unchanged.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: Please clean and tidy the room.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object receiving the cleaning action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adjective ending in な changes its ending to に to become an adverb modifying the following verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form to combine with ください and make a request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence ending that expresses a polite request or suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The sentence combines the adverbial form of the adjective ending in な (きれい + に) to describe how the room is cleaned, together with the request form 'Vて + ください'.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'かたづけてくださいませんか' is used, the request sounds more polite and gentle.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If the negative form 'かたづけないでください' is used, the sentence means 'please do not clean up.'
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the adjective ending な to に when modifying a verb, and may confuse it with きれい かたづける.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q5.kobun.cn: Vて + ください / Aな + に + V
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: I used a 1,000-yen bill to buy 800-yen snacks and received 200 yen in change.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.sk: Amount で、Amount の N を Vて、Amount の N を Vました
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the amount of money or the tool used for payment.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の connects the amount of money to the noun for the snacks.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the item being bought.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb uses the て form to connect a sequence of actions in time order.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle の connects the amount of money to the noun for the change.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the object received: the change.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The predicate is in the polite past tense and ends the sentence describing a completed action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The sentence uses the particle で to show the denomination used for payment, and the て form (買って、) to connect two consecutive actions in the purchase.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If '買ってから' is used, the clause clearly emphasizes the order: buying first and then receiving the change.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If に (1,000円に) is used, the sentence changes to mean a fixed price or a change in the amount of money, so it is grammatically incorrect for payment.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particles で and に when talking about money used for shopping. で must be used to indicate the payment amount.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: Ken always works very hard and seriously.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Ken as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing that an action happens continuously or regularly.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An adjective ending in な changes its ending to に to function as an adverb modifying his attitude toward work.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb uses the ています form to show a habitual state or work that happens regularly.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The sentence combines the frequency adverb 'いつも' and the adverbial adjective 'まじめに' with the tense '〜ています' to describe Ken's everyday work style and habits.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If the simple present form 'はたらきます' is used, the sentence only states a general fact or plan. It does not clearly show the habitual state expressed by ています.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'まじめな' is used, it must come before a noun, such as まじめな人. It cannot modify the following verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the endings な and に when changing an adjective ending in な into an adverb modifying a verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or a respectful title
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: Aな + に + V / Vて + います
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: There was an earthquake this morning, so I was very scared.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.sk: Time 、 N が Vて + Aい (past tense)
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A time noun used as an adverb to show when the event happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks a natural phenomenon that occurs.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb uses the て form as a connector showing the natural cause that leads to the feeling in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the short past tense to show fear felt at that time.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The て form of the verb (あって) is used to show an objective cause that leads to a mental state or feeling in the following clause (こわかった).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'じしんがあったから / あったので' is used, the cause-and-effect explanation is clearer and more subjective than the て form.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If the present form 'こわい' is used, the sentence describes fear in the present, not the fear felt when the earthquake happened in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often remember only that the て form is used to list actions, and forget that the て form is also commonly used to state a cause leading to a feeling.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + 感情・状態を表す表現
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: I made a hotel reservation for tomorrow.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「の」 connects the time noun 「あした」 to modify the noun 「ホテル」 that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「の」 connects the noun 「ホテル」 to modify the noun 「よやく」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「を」 marks the direct recipient of the action 「しました」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 「する」 in the polite past form serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The sentence uses the particle sequence 「の」 to gradually narrow the scope from time to place and then to the reservation. The predicate uses the phrase 「N をしました」 to show that the action was completed in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It only describes the existing state of having an appointment or reservation, without stressing that the speaker made it personally, as in よやくをしました.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: In Japanese, time or place modifiers must always come before the main noun they modify and connect to it with 「の」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: Recently, I have often been away from home.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The time adverb at the beginning of the sentence sets the time for the whole action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the noun 「家」 as the object affected by the phrase 「るすにする」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「に」 combines with the noun 「るす」 to create a resulting state for the verb 「する」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb 「する」 directly modifies the abstract noun 「こと」 that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The action is nominalized with 「こと」 and combined with the particle 「が」 to serve as the subject of the quantity predicate。「おおいです」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending い combines with 「です」 as the main predicate, forming the structure 「〜ことが多い」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The structure 「〜ことが多い」 uses the dictionary form nominalized by 「こと」, together with the particle 「が」, to show that something happens many times in reality.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes occasionally doing something or having done something before, with a much lower frequency than 〜ことが多い.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes a fixed rule, custom, or schedule, rather than a personal habit or frequency.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Before 「ことが多い」, there must be a verb in its plain form (or ない form). Learners often mistakenly use the past form when talking about recent events.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことが多い
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「の」 connects the time noun 「きょう」 to modify the noun 「テスト」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「は」 comes after the noun to identify the topic being evaluated in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending な 「かんたん」 combines with the polite past ending 「でした」 to form the evaluative predicate.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The sentence topic is clearly narrowed by the phrase 「きょうのテストは」, and the predicate uses the adjective ending な in the polite past form 「でした」 to evaluate a completed experience.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the same meaning, but it uses the adjective ending い 「やさしい」 in the past tense and focuses more on the level of difficulty than the simple structure of かんたん.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: The present tense does not show that the test took place and that the speaker finished it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: The adjective ending な has the polite past form 「〜でした」, and learners often confuse it with the ending 「〜かったです」 used with adjectives ending in い.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「が」 marks the subject in which the breakdown occurs naturally.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun 「こしょう」 combines with the verb 「する」 in the polite past form to serve as the predicate describing a breakdown.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: The sentence describes an objective event that happened to the car, so it uses the subject particle 「が」 with the verb for machine failure 「こしょうしました」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: The verb meaning “break” or “be broken” is used for all objects and household items, while こしょう is used only for machines and equipment with moving parts.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: The causative form describes deliberately making the car break down, unlike a failure that happens by itself.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: 「こしょうする」 is used only for machines and equipment, such as cars, washing machines, and watches. It is not used for simple objects such as tables, chairs, or broken dishes.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A relative time noun can come at the beginning of the sentence as an adverb without needing the particle 「に」.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the direct object of the action of quitting.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The transitive verb 「やめる」 in the polite past form serves as the main predicate and shows that a habit ended.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: The time expression 「きょねん」 comes first as an adverb, followed by the direct object with 「を」 and a transitive verb in the past tense showing a completed action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It only describes the present state of not smoking, while やめました emphasizes the decisive action of stopping the habit in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The potential form means “was able to quit smoking,” emphasizing the effort needed to overcome the difficulty of quitting.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Relative time nouns such as きょねん, きのう, and らいしゅう do not take the particle 「に」 after them.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: I will study as hard as I can.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: It acts as an adverb of manner and shows a very high level of effort for the following action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The main predicate of the sentence, showing the action of studying in the polite form.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The adverbial phrase いっしょうけんめいに comes before the verb and expresses the attitude and determination to perform the action with all one's strength.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: よく focuses more on being regular or hardworking in daily life, while いっしょうけんめい emphasizes the greatest possible effort.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: いっしょうけんめい can be used with に or without に before the verb, without changing the meaning.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A word-forming element meaning looking at, viewing, or observing (kanji root 見).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A word-forming element referring to things or scenes that are viewed (kanji root 物).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: A Sino-Japanese compound made of けん (view) and ぶつ (thing), forming a noun for the activity of visiting and viewing scenery or festivals.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: 観光 has the broad meaning of sightseeing travel, while けんぶつ usually means going to see a specific place, event, or scene.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: けんぶつ can be used independently as a noun or combined with する to make a verb (けんぶつする).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A word-forming element meaning calm, safe, and free from danger (kanji root 安).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A word-forming element meaning the heart or mind (kanji root 心).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: A Sino-Japanese compound made of あん (calm) and しん (mind), describing a relaxed mental state without fear or anxiety.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: 安全 means physical or situational safety, with no danger, while 安心 means psychological and emotional peace of mind.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: あんしん can be a noun and a な-ending adjective (あんしんな), and it can also become a verb when combined with する (あんしんする).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The stem of an -i adjective meaning detailed, precise, or made up of small pieces.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The ending of an -i adjective in its plain affirmative form.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: An -i adjective used to describe small size, detailed content, or coins and money of small value.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It means large and is completely opposite in size and scale.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: Learners must clearly distinguish “small change” (細かいお金) from “little money” (少ないお金).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The stem of a group 2 intransitive verb describing an object that is torn or has a hole.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form ending of a group 2 verb.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: A group 2 intransitive verb showing that paper, cloth, bags, or clothes are torn or damaged.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It is a transitive verb used with the particle を to show the intentional action of tearing or ripping something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the difference between the intransitive verb 破れる, which takes が, and the transitive verb 破る, which takes を.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: How do you say “oishii” in English?
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The word or phrase being asked about is made the topic of the sentence with the particle は.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the means or language used for expression.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word なん combines with the particle と to quote the content of a statement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 言う in the ます form combines with the question particle か to make a polite question.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses the particle は to make the vocabulary item the topic, the particle で to show the language tool, and なんと as the quotation component for the verb 言う.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle に means translating “into Vietnamese” and usually goes with 訳す/直す. It is unnatural with 言う.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse using the particle に instead of で when asking how to say something “in a particular language.”
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: N ＋ で ＋ なんと言う
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi: If you catch a cold, you should take medicine and go to bed early.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The object used with the verb 引いたら forms the phrase 風邪を引く (catch a cold).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb uses the たら form to express the condition “if/after catching a cold.”
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The direct object of the action of drinking or taking (飲んで).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb uses the て form to connect actions in time order.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The adverb modifies the action of going to bed (ねた).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The past-form verb combines with ほうが to form a comparison showing the better choice.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The evaluative predicate combines with ほうがいい to create a gentle advice pattern.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: The sentence uses the conditional 『〜たら』 in the first clause to set an assumption, then uses the 『〜て』 form to connect the action of taking medicine before giving advice 『〜たほうがいい』 at the end.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Used to advise that someone 'should not do something' (e.g., はやくねないほうがいい: should not go to bed early).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: It gently suggests trying something rather than giving direct advice.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly change the verb before ほうがいい into the dictionary form (Vる) instead of the past form (Vた) when advising someone what to do.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q10.kobun.cn: Vた / Vない + ほうがいい(です)
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi: A: “What happened? You look rather pale.” - B: “Actually, yesterday my senior forced me to drink a lot of alcohol.”
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.sk:
A: どうしたんですか + 顔色 が 悪いですね
B: N(person) に + N(thing) を + V(使役受身)んです
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: The mark that opens speaker A's line.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern 〜んですか is used to ask about the cause when an unusual sign is noticed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The subject of the adjective 悪い.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The evaluative predicate comments on the condition of the complexion and uses the particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: The mark that opens speaker B's line.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: An introductory adverb used when explaining a truth or the reason behind something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb of time referring to an event that has already happened.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle に marks the agent who forced the action in a causative-passive sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.8.n: An adverb of quantity modifying the amount of alcohol the speaker was forced to drink.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.9.n: The direct object of the action of drinking, used with the particle を.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.10.n: The verb is in the causative-passive form (使役受身), expressing being forced to do something one does not want to do. The ending んです provides an explanation.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.cn:
Group 1: V(a)せられる / V(a)される (except the ending す)
Group 2: V(remove る)させられる
Group 3: くる→こさせられる / する→させられる
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: The causative-passive form (飲まされた) expresses reluctance and discomfort when another person (先輩に) forces the speaker to drink alcohol. It combines with the ending 『〜んです』 to explain the reason to speaker A.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows gratitude because a senior gave the speaker alcohol or treated them to drinks, which is the opposite of feeling forced.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.1.d: The ordinary passive form (someone else drank the alcohol), which does not show that the speaker was forced to drink.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the causative form (飲ませる - make or let someone else do something) with the causative-passive form (飲まされる - be made to do something by someone else).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi: I hope the weather will be nice tomorrow.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.sk: N(time) は + Aい N に + V辞書形 + といいですね
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes 'tomorrow' the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い directly modifies the noun 天気.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に combines with the verb なる to show the result of a change in the weather.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と follows the dictionary form to express a condition in the hope pattern 〜といい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜といいですね is used to express a wish for something good to happen in nature.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: The sentence pattern 『〜といいですね』 is used with the dictionary-form verb (なると) to express a wish or hope that a natural event beyond human control, such as the weather, will develop favorably.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Used only to express one's own wish to actively do something; it is not used for natural events such as the weather.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.1.d: Used to wish for a specific person or thing to perform an action for oneself; it is not used with nature.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use 〜たい to wish for good weather (*天気がよくなりたい), while the grammatically correct pattern is 〜といい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: V普通形 / Aい / Aな / Nだ + といい(ですね)
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi: Thank you for helping me with my report yesterday.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.sk: N(time) は + N を + Vてくれて、+ ありがとうございました
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the time as the topic that introduces the event.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The direct object of the action of helping (手伝って).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜てくれる uses the て form to connect sentences and show the reason for thanking someone for doing something helpful.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate expresses gratitude for an action completed in the past.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: Use 『〜てくれる』 when another person does an action that benefits you, then use the 『〜て』 form to connect directly to the expression of thanks 『〜てくれて、ありがとうございました』.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes an action that you do to help someone else; it is not used when thanking someone for helping you.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: Receiving help (the てもらう form); it can also be used in thanks, but focuses on yourself as the receiver of the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse てくれる (someone else does something for you) with てあげる (you do something for someone else), which leads to mistakes when giving thanks.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q13.kobun.cn: Vて + くれる / くれて、ありがとう(ございました)
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi: On days off, I usually do things such as taking walks and playing games...
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun 休み modifies the noun 日 that follows through the particle の.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the time 'day off' the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The object used with the verb 散歩をする (take a walk).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜たり lists the first representative action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: This listing clause is repeated exactly as in the exercise sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The object used with the verb ゲームをする (play games).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern 〜たり lists the second representative action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: This listing clause is repeated exactly as in the exercise sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb します comes at the end of the sentence to complete the action-listing structure 〜たり〜たりする.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.cn: Vた + り、Vた + りする / Aい(remove い) + かったり / Aな・N + だったり
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: The structure 『〜たり〜たりする』 is used to list several representative actions from among the many things done on a day off. It ends with the verb します.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Used to list all actions in time order, without the selective representative meaning of 〜たり.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: Mainly used to list nouns (NとかNとか); for verbs, the grammatically correct form is 〜たり.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the verb into the past form (Vた) before り, or forget to put the verb する/します at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi: A: “Have you read this document yet?” - B: “No, I still haven't read it.”
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: The mark that opens speaker A's line.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing that an action has been completed or has reached a certain point.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun 資料.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The direct object of reading (読みましたか).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-form verb combines with the question particle か to ask whether the action has been completed.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The mark that opens speaker B's line.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: A negative word used to answer a question that checks information.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.7.n: An adverb used with the negative form 〜ていません to show that an action has not happened up to the present.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern 〜ていません is used to give a negative answer to the question 'Have you done V yet?' (still have not done it).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: もう + Vましたか → まだ + Vていません (do not use Vませんでした)
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: When asked whether an action has been completed using 『もう〜ましたか』, the negative answer must use 『まだ〜ていません』 to show that the action has not been done up to the present.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect in Japanese because ませんでした refers to something that was not done in the past, not to the meaning 'still have not done it.'
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses the intention 'will not read it anymore,' which is completely different from 'have not read it yet.'
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: Learners often answer the question 'Have you done V yet?' with the negative past form (Vませんでした) instead of the correct structure, Vていません.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi:
【At the convenience store】
Tanaka: 'Excuse me, I would like to buy some chewing gum...'
Staff member: 'If you mean chewing gum, it is over there.'
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase in brackets shows the location where the dialogue takes place.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The speaker's name, together with an apology, is used to begin the conversation politely.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action the speaker wants to buy.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the desire form Vたい combines with んですが to make a tactful request for help.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.4.vi: Staff member: 'If you mean chewing gum,
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle なら takes up the topic just mentioned by the other person and gives helpful information.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に identifies the location where an object exists.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The grammar pattern Vてある shows that an object has been intentionally placed and is already in that state.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: The staff member immediately takes up the topic just mentioned by the other person with the particle なら ('ガム') and gives directions as a solution, using Vてある to show that the goods have already been put on display.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If Vている is used, it describes an action in progress or a habit. It does not emphasize that the goods have already been prepared as Vてある does.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: The pattern なら comes directly after a noun, without needing to add だ or な.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ なら
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi: That person said they would come, but they did not come.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person performing the action the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と is used to quote the content of speech.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate of the subordinate clause uses the past short form before the conjunction のに.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The conjunction のに connects two contrasting clauses and shows disappointment or surprise when things do not happen as expected.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is in the polite past negative form and describes the actual result.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: The structure のに is chosen to express the contrast between the promise or expectation in the first clause and what actually happened in the second clause. It carries a tone of blame or regret.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply connects two clauses that are objectively contrasting and does not contain the strong feeling of dissatisfaction or disappointment found in のに.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows the reason leading to a result, completely changing the relationship between the two actions from contrast.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: When a noun or a present affirmative -na adjective is connected to のに, な must be added (for example: 暇なのに, 雨なのに).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな (な)・N (な) ＋ のに
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi: Because I could not travel much last year, I plan to travel a lot this year.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は sets a time point as the background for comparison with this year.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb used with a negative form to show a small amount or degree.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the purpose of the movement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb uses the past negative potential form and combines with ので to give an objective reason.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は sets a time point as the topic for comparison.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing quantity that modifies the action of going.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb uses the volitional form and combines with the particle と to introduce the intended action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern 〜と思っています expresses an intention that was formed earlier and is still continuing.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The first clause uses ので to explain why the speaker could not travel much last year. The second clause uses the volitional form with と思っています to express a firm intention or plan that has been developing for this year.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply states a plan, while 〜と思っています emphasizes a thought or determination that arose or has been kept in the speaker's mind.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses an intention that has just arisen at the time of speaking, rather than one developed earlier like 〜と思っています.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: The verb before と思っています must be changed to the volitional form (Vよう/Vおう). The dictionary form and past form cannot be used.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: V意向形 ＋ と思っている／と思っています
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The limiting particle だけ comes after the noun that is the object of the writing ability.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 書く is turned into a noun with こと, then combines with the particle が and できます to form a potential structure.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate shows the ability to perform the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: The pattern 〜ことができる expresses ability and combines with the particle だけ to emphasize the limitation that only that action is possible.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means 'only,' but しか must be used with a negative verb (ひらがなしか書くことができません) and carries more regret.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses 'nothing but' or repeated action and is not used to simply limit ability like だけ.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: After だけ, the particles を or が may be omitted without changing the grammatical meaning.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる／ことができます
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: Let's all watch TV or do something similar.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で shows the group or number of people taking part in the action together.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun used as the object being suggested.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle でも gives a representative example as a gentle suggestion or proposal.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The ending 〜ましょう is used to invite the other person to do something together.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The particle で after みんな shows the group acting together. The particle でも presents TV as a gentle suggestion, combined with the inviting ending 〜ましょう.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If を (テレビを見ましょう) is used, watching TV is named as the only choice, so it lacks the open suggestion expressed by でも.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It politely asks for the other person's opinion ('Shall we watch TV?'), while 〜ましょう is more direct and inviting.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Here, the particle でも means giving a suggested example ('for example...'), not 'even' or 'although it is'.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: Yamashita is sure to return tomorrow.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person being judged the topic.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the formal noun はず.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern はずです expresses a confident judgment based on clear evidence or reasons.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The topic 山下さん is assigned an action occurring at the time あした, ending with はずです to show the speaker's high level of confidence based on an existing schedule or other evidence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It is an ordinary guess that does not necessarily have evidence, while はず requires the speaker to have a reliable reason or basis.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a low-confidence guess, about 50%, while はず expresses a very high level of confidence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: When connected to a noun, the pattern はずだ must add the particle の (N の はず), while the adjective ending な keeps な unchanged (Aな な はず).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or other polite title
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな (な)・N (の) ＋ はずだ／はずです
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: This snack is easy to eat.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.sk: この N は ＋ Vます(omit ます)やすいです
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun おかし that follows.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the noun the topic being described or evaluated.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: Use the verb form ます, remove ます, and add やすい to show that an action is easy to do.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: Vます(remove ます) ＋ やすい／やすいです
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: The topic このおかし is described through the predicate combined with the ending やすい, meaning that the snack is easy and pleasant to eat.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Shows difficulty or an obstacle when performing an action (食べにくい = difficult to eat), and is the direct opposite pattern of やすい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Besides meaning “easy to do,” at a higher level やすい can also show a negative tendency that is likely to occur (for example: 壊れやすい = easy to break, 風邪をひきやすい = easy to catch a cold).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: When a verb is combined with やすい, it must be changed to the ます form, and then the ending ます is removed (for example: 食べます → 食べやすい).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: I went out without turning off the electricity, and I also left the door unlocked like that.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of turning off.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The ないで verb form describes not doing one action while continuing with another.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of opening.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern たまま describes keeping a state unchanged while carrying out the next action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The main verb in the て form connects to the auxiliary verb showing an unintended action at the end of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern てしまう expresses regret about accidentally doing something unwanted.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The sentence combines two unfinished states using Vないで and Vたまま before leaving the house, and ends with てしまいました to show regret and carelessness.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It also describes leaving a state unchanged, but it follows V after removing ます and has a stronger blaming or critical tone.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It only shows a simple cause-and-effect relationship (because the electricity was not turned off...), and is not used to show an accompanying state like 〜ないで.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Be careful not to confuse Vないで (not doing A but doing B) with Vなくて (stating a cause or reason).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Nの ＋ まま / Vて ＋ しまう
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: I will throw it away later, so please gather the rubbish for me in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A time phrase showing when the action of throwing away the rubbish will happen.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.vi: because I will throw it away later,
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjunction から connects a reason clause that explains the request in the following clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the gathering action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern ておく shows doing an action in advance to prepare for a later purpose.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern ください follows the て form to make a polite request.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses から to explain that the rubbish will be thrown away later. The second clause uses the pattern ておく together with ください to ask the other person to gather the rubbish in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows trying an action, and does not mean preparing in advance for the future like 〜ておく.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It only describes a state that was completed in advance and is still maintained. It is not used to order or ask someone to prepare something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse ておく (doing something in advance) with てある (a state that someone has already prepared).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ おく / Vて ＋ ください
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: Just as I was about to leave the house, it started to rain.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を is used with the verb for leaving (出る) to show the starting point or the place left behind.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The past form of the pattern ようとする modifies とき and describes the moment when someone was just about to do something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun phrase とき combines with the particle に to identify the time when the unexpected event in the next clause occurred.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of a natural phenomenon.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern てくる describes a natural phenomenon beginning to appear and develop.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: The structure Vようとする shows the moment just before an action begins and sets the time for the unexpected event that interrupts it in the next clause.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows the moment just after an action has been completed. This is the opposite of 〜ようとしたときに, which means that the person has not done it yet and has only just decided to do it.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows an action in progress and does not emphasize the moment just before it begins, as 〜ようとしたときに does.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Distinguish Vようとする (about to do something immediately) from Vつもりだ (a general future intention or plan).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: V意向形（よう・おう形） ＋ とする / Vて ＋ くる
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: A: “Shall we go to a hot spring tomorrow?” — B: “Sounds good. May I bring my younger brother too?”
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A time word at the beginning of A’s dialogue that states when they will meet.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the destination of the movement action 行く.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜ませんか is used to make a polite invitation or suggestion.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: An exclamatory sentence showing agreement and enthusiasm about the other person’s invitation.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle も shows that another person is being added to the group taking part (bringing the younger brother too).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜ていいですか (with も omitted) is used to ask the other person for permission to do something.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The dialogue uses 〜ませんか to make a polite invitation. The other speaker accepts it and then uses 〜ていいですか to ask permission for a third person to come along.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used when the speaker voluntarily offers to do something for the other person, rather than inviting them to go together as in 〜ませんか.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It asks about a prohibition (is it not allowed?), and does not have the gentle permission-seeking meaning of 〜ていいですか.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: In spoken conversation, the permission pattern 〜ていいですか often omits the particle も from the standard form 〜てもいいですか.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: Vます ＋ ませんか / Vて ＋ （も）いいですか
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: I have always wanted my father to give up drinking.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the speaker as the topic and the person who has the wish in the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person whom the speaker wants to perform the action.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of giving up (やめる).
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜てほしい expresses a wish for another person to do something. It combines with the particle と to introduce the content of the thought.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 思う in the progressive form describes the subject’s lasting thought and long-held wish.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The structure N2にVてほしい expresses a wish for person N2 to do action V. It is used with と思っています to show that this feeling has been held for a long time.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used only to express the speaker’s wish to do something personally, not another person’s action as in 〜てほしい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It also means wanting someone to do something, but it places more emphasis on the speaker wanting to receive that action as help or a favor.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use 〜たい when they want another person to do something, although Japanese requires N に Vてほしい.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ほしい / 普通形 ＋ と思う
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Is this a family photo? Your older sister looks beautiful and seems gentle.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: の connects 家族 with 写真 and shows that the photo belongs to or is about the family.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: です creates a polite expression, while か at the end turns the sentence into a question.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: This part states the person being described. The comma marks the shift to the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: きれい is an adjective of type な. It changes to きれいで to connect this feature with the next one.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: やさしい removes い and then connects to そうな to form a phrase modifying 人, describing an appearance that seems gentle.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: ですね is placed at the end of the sentence to express an observation and seek the listener’s agreement.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: Aい語幹・Aな語幹・Vます語幹 ＋ そうだ; when modifying a noun: そうな ＋ N
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: 家族の modifies 写真 to identify the type of photo. The sentence then shifts to a comment about お姉さん. The two features, きれい and やさしそう, are connected by で and together modify 人. ですね makes the comment softer and more natural.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If やさしそうな is replaced with やさしいような, the meaning leans toward an inference or comparison based on evidence, rather than only a visual impression.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If やさしいらしい is used, it means that the speaker has heard that she is gentle. It does not necessarily describe something the speaker directly senses.
default.q.goukakumoshi1_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may confuse そうな in やさしそうな with そうだ meaning “it is said.” Here, it describes an appearance that seems to be so.
